title: Sequential reading of a stepwise-shortened peptide immobilized on nanopore.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the Supplementary Data zip MOESM3 (1.4 MB, no login needed): it holds tPAL_decoder.m (MATLAB code), a readme, training_set.xlsx (4,519 rows x 13 columns: 11 per-event current features in pA (picoamperes) or time, a Label column with 16 three-residue N-terminal classes, and Source_Peptide with 24 model peptides; 0 missing values, 5 exact duplicate rows), predicting_KTREFTRSC.xlsx (9 unlabelled sheets, one per digestion stage, 12 to 954 events each) and the decoder outputs. I also opened source-data xlsx files MOESM7 to MOESM16, which are small per-figure tables (t-SNE coordinates, mean current over 3 trials, etc.).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Full text is paywalled and not in Europe PMC, so I read only the abstract and a search snippet saying the decoder code and training data are in Supplementary Data. I did not read the methods, so how events were assigned to digestion stages, the pore and run counts, and the decoder's reported accuracy are unverified. No raw current traces were found in any repository (searched Zenodo, Dryad and GitHub; nothing found).

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: the Springer supplementary zip and source-data xlsx files download without login, even though the article is paywalled.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: training_set.xlsx has a 'Label' column naming the N-terminal 3-mer (three-residue chunk) for each event, e.g. TRS, REF, KTR.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: 11 precomputed numeric features per event (Mean, SD, skew, kurt, toff, Median, Q1, Q3, IQR, mean_max10, mean_max20). Raw current traces are not provided, so only these summaries can be modelled.

a4_units_stated.note: Checked partly: current features are in pA (picoamperes) per the source-data headers 'ΔI (pA)'; toff (dwell time) units are not stated in the training file, probably ms (milliseconds) by magnitude, which is my inference.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: 4,519 labelled events, a classification task, so above the 400-row bar. But 16 classes from only 24 peptides, and FC has 6 events, FEF 55.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Checked: tiny tables; any classifier trains in seconds on CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not compare: paper text unread. The training file and the code's class list (16 classes) agree with each other.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label comes from the experimental design: which synthesized peptide was immobilized, at which enzymatic digestion stage. That is a physical ground truth, not a model output. However label and Source_Peptide are almost one-to-one, so the label is confounded with the experiment it came from.

B1.why: One table, training_set.xlsx, with features, label and source peptide together (checked).

B2.why: xlsx not csv, but read by pandas on the first try with no fixes (checked).

B3.why: One lab and one pore design, but events pooled across separate runs per peptide; no per-run normalization column (checked).

B4.why: No censored or qualitative values; all 11 features are numeric, 0 missing (checked).

B5.why: 5 exact duplicate rows out of 4,519; easy to drop (checked).

B6.why: Readme explains the code, not the feature definitions; toff units unstated (checked).

C1.why: Only result is in-distribution accuracy on 16 classes; no transfer question can be posed with 7 amino acids.

C2.why: Authors' own neural-net decoder plus several 2024–2026 nanopore amino-acid classifiers exist; none benchmarked on this data.

C3.why: Too narrow: 16 three-residue classes from 7 amino acids (K, T, R, E, F, S, C); nothing general to learn.

C4.why: Peptide sequencing by mass spectrometry or Edman degradation is slow and costly; nanopore readout is the cheap alternative.

C5.why: MATLAB decoder code is provided, but no accuracy number seen (paper unread); majority-class baseline is trivial.

D1.why: No open pretrained backbone exists for nanopore peptide event features; ESM-2 embeds sequences, not current signals.

D2.why: Inputs are 11 summary statistics; nothing to freeze-and-head on.

D3.why: Supplementary data licence not stated on the files; assume reuse for research is acceptable.

E1.why: Label nearly equals source peptide, so holding out peptides removes whole classes; only 6 classes appear in 2+ peptides.

E2.why: 24 source peptides but most hold a single class; too few groups per class to hold out.

E3.why: Majority-class baseline is computable: REF is the largest class at 755/4,519 (16.7%) (checked).

E4.why: Source data give 3-trial mean current per stage with standard deviations around 0.1 pA (checked, MOESM13).

E5.why: Positive control: classes with very different mean current (e.g. TRE vs REF stages) must separate easily.

E6.why: Label shuffling and feature ablation (drop toff, keep Mean only) are trivially runnable.

E7.why: No independent nanopore dataset with the same pore, adapter and 3-mer classes was found.

E8.why: Authors' fitcnet decoder and example prediction file are included, so their KTREFTRSC result is reproducible.

G1.why: Only peptide sequences as free text; no protein or database identifiers (checked).

G2.why: No large public resource holds tPAL nanopore readings to join with.

G4.why: Cannot write a bigger combined question; any join would be decoration.

H1.why: Every event is labelled with a true class; no failed or misassigned events reported in the training file.

H2.why: One lab, one engineered pore, 24 synthetic peptides built from 7 amino acids (checked).

H3.why: Claim is precise: classifies 16 N-terminal 3-mers from synthetic peptides on this one pore setup.

H4.why: Narrow residue set is evident from the files; whether the paper flags it is unread.

I1.why: Nanopore protein-sequencing groups, but they would use their own new data, not this table.

I2.why: A better classifier on these 16 classes would not change any experiment.

I3.why: Per-stage classification accuracy roughly matches the sequence-decoding goal.

I4.why: The authors' decoder already reaches near-certain per-stage calls (0.89–1.0 class probability in their output file); a simple classifier suffices.

J1.why: Small tabular classification only; no splits, transfer learning or backbone to learn.

J2.why: Current-level intuition is specialised but per-class means are easy to sanity-check.

J3.why: A reanalysis note is possible, but of little interest.

J4.why: Could be finished in a day; no budget defined.

existing_models.name: tPAL_decoder (this paper): one-hidden-layer neural network (MATLAB fitcnet, 100 units) on 11 event features, plus graph assembly
existing_models.score_and_split: Accuracy not seen (paper unread); its included output assigns the correct 3-mer at 8 of 8 stages of KTREFTRSC with 0.89–1.0 probability.

existing_models.name: Cu(II)-functionalized MspA classifier, Nature Methods 2024 ('Real-time detection of 20 amino acids...')
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond search snippet; identifies all 20 amino acids with machine learning.

existing_models.name: MspA-NTA-Ni nanopore classifier, Nature Biotechnology 2026 ('An engineered nanopore identifies saccharides, amino acids, peptides and ribonucleotides')
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet: validation accuracy up to 97.4% within the studied dataset (split not stated).

existing_models.name: Multi-modal transformer for nanopore blockade signals (arXiv 2607.20323)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet: beats prior methods by over 10 points on a 42-peptide benchmark; near-perfect on a 20-amino-acid dataset.

existing_models.name: SEDA-Former, deep temporal model for nanopore identification (Nature Communications 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet: evaluated on glycoside, ginsenoside, DNA and cholic-acid nanopore benchmarks.

backbone.name: none: no pretrained model exists for nanopore peptide event summary features
backbone.licence: Supplementary data licence not stated on files

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not write one; there is no public resource of comparable nanopore readings to join.

controls.positive_control: Classes with clearly different mean blockade current (e.g. REF vs TRE stages) must be separated near-perfectly; the authors' decoder should reproduce its own KTREFTRSC calls.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the Label column and confirm accuracy drops to the 16.7% majority-class rate.
controls.external_validation: None: no independent dataset with the same pore and classes.

honest_claim_h3: A classifier could assign one of 16 N-terminal three-residue chunks, built from 7 amino acids in 24 synthetic peptides, to events from one lab's engineered MspA pore, and nothing beyond that.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use summary statistics of the electrical current while a peptide sits in a nanopore to predict which three amino acids are at its tip.
plain_idea.train_on: Eleven numbers per event (mean current, spread, shape, dwell time) for 4,519 events from 24 synthetic peptides (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Which of 16 three-residue chunks is at the peptide's front end, known because the authors synthesized each peptide and trimmed it one residue at a time with an enzyme.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: the authors' own simple classifier already decodes it, and only 7 amino acids are covered, so nothing transfers to real proteins.

more_or_better_data.why: 4,519 events over 16 classes from 7 amino acids, smaller and narrower than the 20-amino-acid and 42-peptide nanopore benchmarks found in search.

confidence_score.why: Source data give 3-trial standard deviations per stage, but the authors' decoder already outputs class probabilities.

models_beatable.why: Their 2026 neural network already gives 0.89–1.0 probability for the right class at each stage in the shipped output; little room left.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No joinable new data measures the same quantity on the same pore; the condition 'same assay, more data' fails.

ml_idea: Reclassify the 16 N-terminal 3-mer classes from 11 event features and test generalization to held-out peptides; infeasible because labels are nearly one-to-one with source peptides and only 7 amino acids appear.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 4,519 x 11 table size; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Cross-tabulate Label by Source_Peptide (done): 10 of 16 classes come from a single peptide, so no honest held-out-peptide split exists.

verdict_reason: Data downloads and is tidy (4,519 labelled events), but it is a 16-class toy set from 7 amino acids in 24 synthetic peptides, with labels confounded with the experiment that produced them. There is no pretrained backbone, no join partner and no external set, and the authors' own classifier already solves it.
